g9-economics-ue1-t1.overview: Meaning of Economics sits inside Introducing Economics. Introduction to economics is the focus of Unit 1 of Grade 9 Economics in the Ethiopian (FDRE Ministry of Education) curriculum. First, it defines economics as the social science of allocating scarce resources to satisfy unlimited human wants. Then it separates the two main branches, microeconomics and macroeconomics, and shows how economists reason and judge. Finally, it presents the three decision-making units that drive an economy. Students will also learn how this introduction to economics applies to real-life situations and everyday choices.
objectives: Define economics and explain its nature as a science and an art.
Distinguish microeconomics from macroeconomics.
Describe the deductive and inductive methods of study.
Compare positive and normative economics.
Identify the three decision-making units and their objectives.
g9-economics-ue1-t1.simple:
Meaning of Economics in plain words. The exam wants you to recognise the core ideas, not to memorise whole paragraphs. Focus on:
  • First, economics as a social science that studies the efficient allocation of scarce resources.
  • The origin of the word from the Greek oikonomia, meaning the management of a household.
  • Then the nature of economics as both a science and an art.
  • Also why a deep knowledge of economics helps a society tackle poverty, unemployment, and inflation.
g9-economics-ue1-t1.detailed:
Meaning of Economics — the essentials. First, economics as a social science that studies the efficient allocation of scarce resources. The origin of the word from the Greek oikonomia, meaning the management of a household. Then the nature of economics as both a science and an art. Also why a deep knowledge of economics helps a society tackle poverty, unemployment, and inflation.

What the MoE expects you to be able to do:

  • Define economics and explain its nature as a science and an art.
  • Distinguish microeconomics from macroeconomics.
  • Describe the deductive and inductive methods of study.
  • Compare positive and normative economics.
  • Identify the three decision-making units and their objectives.

g9-economics-ue1-t3.simple:
Methods and Approaches of Studying Economics in plain words. The exam wants you to recognise the core ideas, not to memorise whole paragraphs. Focus on:
  • First, the deductive method, which reasons from general principles to particular facts.
  • Then the inductive method, which reasons from particular observations to a general rule.
  • Also positive economics, which describes the world as it is, using facts.
  • Finally, normative economics, which judges what the economy ought to be.

g9-economics-ue1-t4.simple:
Decision Making Units in plain words. The exam wants you to recognise the core ideas, not to memorise whole paragraphs. Focus on:
  • First, households, the owners of land, labour, capital, and entrepreneurship, who earn rent, wages, interest, and profit.

  • Finally, how these three units interact across an economy.
